### Govee {#govee}

[govee.com](https://govee.com) · Driver `govee`

**Devices tracked:** 4 supported

> Discovered by UDP multicast on the Govee LAN protocol; LAN devices stream RGB frames directly. The Govee Developer API v1 adds cloud inventory enrichment and a control fallback for cloud-only SKUs such as bulbs. A built-in capability database maps each SKU to its LED count, segment topology, and protocol flags.

#### Supported (4)

| Device | Type | Driver | Transport | Notes |

| Govee RGBIC LED Strip | LED strip | `govee` | UDP | Per-segment RGBIC strips streamed over the Govee LAN protocol. Select SKUs (H619A, H70B1) also support Razer streaming for higher frame rates. |
| Govee RGBIC Light Bars | Lightbar | `govee` | UDP | Govee Flow and Flow Pro desktop light bars and similar segmented RGBIC bars. |
| Govee RGBIC TV Backlight | LED strip | `govee` | UDP | Immersion and Envisual TV backlight kits. The backlight strip streams over the Govee LAN protocol; the bundled camera module is not used. |

### LIFX {#lifx}

[lifx.com](https://www.lifx.com) · Driver `lifx`

**Devices tracked:** 9 supported

> Driven over the official LIFX LAN protocol on UDP port 56700: discovered by broadcast GetService or configured IPs, with no account or pairing. Zone counts and tile geometry are read from each device at connect. Experimental: tested against the lifx-emulator project, not yet verified on real LIFX hardware.

### Twinkly {#twinkly}

[twinkly.com](https://twinkly.com) · Driver `twinkly`

**Devices tracked:** 5 supported · 2 known

> Driven over the local REST API (login and verify handshake, gestalt, LED layout) and the real-time UDP frame protocol on port 7777, in datagram version 1, 2, or 3 by firmware. Discovered by the UDP discovery datagram on port 5555 or configured IPs; no account or pairing. Every LED is addressable, and the layout mapped in the Twinkly app becomes spatial positions. Experimental: tested against an in-repo fake device, not yet verified on real Twinkly hardware.

#### Supported (5)

| Device | Type | Driver | Transport | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Twinkly Curtain and Wall | Other | `twinkly` | UDP | Parallel-string curtains such as the 210-LED RGBW Special Edition. The 2D layout from the Twinkly app sets each LED's position. Experimental, unverified on hardware. |
| Twinkly Flex and Line | LED strip | `twinkly` | UDP | Flexible tubes and light lines, streamed per LED in wiring order or along the mapped layout. Experimental, unverified on hardware. |
| Twinkly Matrix and Tree | Other | `twinkly` | UDP | Matrix lights and pre-lit trees; 3D tree layouts are viewed from the front. Experimental, unverified on hardware. |
| Twinkly Squares | Other | `twinkly` | UDP | 8x8 RGB panels, up to 16 per chain. Map the panels in the Twinkly app first so the layout carries their arrangement. Experimental, unverified on hardware. |
| Twinkly Strings | LED strip | `twinkly` | UDP | Generation I and II strings, RGB and RGBW, including Festoon, Cluster, and Icicle. LED count, profile, and firmware are read from the device. Experimental, unverified on hardware. |

#### Known (2)

| Device | Type | Transport | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Twinkly Gold Edition (AWW) | LED strip | UDP | Amber, warm, and cold white LEDs (AWW profile). The per-LED byte order is undocumented, so these are skipped until it is. |
| Twinkly Pro controllers | ARGB controller | HTTP | Pro controllers speak a separate /xled/v2 API that the driver does not implement yet. |

### WiZ {#wiz}

[wizconnected.com](https://www.wizconnected.com) · Driver `wiz`

**Devices tracked:** 4 supported

> Driven over the local WiZ UDP JSON API on port 38899: discovered by a registration broadcast or configured IPs, classified from the module name, and streamed one setPilot per frame. Every WiZ device is one color. Homes set to Only verified controls need the home signing key from the WiZ app. Experimental: tested against an in-repo fake device, not yet verified on real WiZ hardware.

### Yeelight {#yeelight}

[yeelight.com](https://www.yeelight.com) · Driver `yeelight`

**Devices tracked:** 4 supported

> Driven over the official Yeelight LAN Control protocol: SSDP-style search on UDP port 1982 or configured IPs, JSON commands on TCP port 55443, and music mode, where the light connects back to Hypercolor and the 60-commands-per-minute quota is lifted. Every Yeelight light is one color. LAN Control must be switched on per light in the Yeelight app. Experimental: tested against an in-repo fake device, not yet verified on real Yeelight hardware.

#### Supported (4)

| Device | Type | Driver | Transport | LEDs | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Yeelight Color Bulbs | Other | `yeelight` | TCP | 1 | Color bulbs (color, color1 to color6), one color and brightness per frame through set_scene, streamed in music mode. Experimental, unverified on hardware. |
| Yeelight Lamps | Other | `yeelight` | TCP | 1 | Bedside lamps and color desk lamps with LAN Control. Some Xiaomi-branded lamps no longer offer LAN Control. Experimental, unverified on hardware. |
| Yeelight Light Strips | LED strip | `yeelight` | TCP | 1 | Lightstrip and Lightstrip Plus (stripe, strip1 to strip6) as one color. Per-segment Lightstrip Pro control is undocumented and not driven. Experimental, unverified on hardware. |
| Yeelight White and Ceiling Lights | Other | `yeelight` | TCP | 1 | White and tunable white bulbs and ceiling lights follow the effect's brightness; background lights are not driven. Experimental, unverified on hardware. |
